page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Eadsv7 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The CPU includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Conversely, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores, fall within the average tier (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, as well as Passmark memory and database operations, also demonstrate average performance. For language model workloads, text generation using a small 135M model is strong (top 25%), while prompt processing with a medium 7B model is weak (bottom 25%).

Given its high memory density of 16.0 GB per vCPU and bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The high single-core performance makes it suitable for applications bound by single-threaded execution speed. Recommended workloads include memory-optimized databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference tasks.
